name: Digital Asset Accounting
blurb: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation, token valuation, contract auditing, decentralised treasuries and impairment.
title: Digital Asset Accounting
answer: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation, token valuation, contract auditing, decentralised treasuries and impairment.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation
children.blurb: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation is the practice of matching on-chain activity against the accounting records a business keeps in its general ledger.

children.name: Valuing Illiquid Tokens
children.blurb: Valuing illiquid tokens covers the problem of putting a defensible number on a digital asset that has no reliable market price.

children.name: Auditing Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Auditing smart contracts means reviewing the code that runs on a blockchain to check that it does what its authors claim and nothing more.

children.name: Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries
children.blurb: Accounting for decentralised treasuries covers the recording, measurement and reporting of assets held and controlled by a protocol, a DAO or a similar on chain entity rather than by a conventional company.

children.name: Impairment of Unique Digital Assets
children.blurb: Impairment of unique digital assets covers the accounting question of when a non-fungible token, a unique on-chain collectible, or a similar one-of-a-kind digital holding has lost value and must be written down.

sections.body: Digital asset accounting is the work of making on chain activity legible to ordinary accounting systems, and AI is doing the tedious parts of that translation. Software reads wallet addresses, transaction hashes and token movements, then matches them against entries in a general ledger, flagging breaks for a human to review. Models also scan smart contract code for common flaws before a contract goes live, and they help estimate what a token is worth when no reliable market price exists. The work is less about prediction and more about classification, matching and evidence gathering at a scale a person cannot read by hand.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Reconciliation is the most mature area, because the underlying data is public and the matching rules are mechanical, though chains reorganise and bridges obscure the path of an asset, so breaks still occur. Token valuation remains genuinely hard: for illiquid or unique assets there may be no comparable sale, and a model can only organise the assumptions a valuer supplies. Smart contract auditing with AI catches known vulnerability patterns but cannot prove a contract is safe, and it misses economic and governance flaws that have nothing to do with code. Impairment testing inherits all of this uncertainty, since a write down depends on a value that may itself be a judgement call. Nothing here replaces an accountant's sign off or an auditor's opinion.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Start with Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation for the plumbing that turns raw chain data into ledger entries, since every other page depends on that record being complete. Valuing Illiquid Tokens then takes those holdings and asks what they are worth when markets are thin, which feeds directly into Impairment of Unique Digital Assets, where a single non fungible item must be tested for a fall in value. Auditing Smart Contracts sits slightly apart, aimed at the code that moves the assets rather than the assets themselves, and is the page to read when the question is whether a protocol can be trusted to behave as described. Accounting for Decentralised Treasuries brings the other four together, because a treasury holds tokens, executes through contracts and must report a position that is both real and valued. Read that last page as the applied case that shows how the pieces constrain one another.
